heading: CHAPTER XII.
title: HOW MANY KINDS OF SOLDIERY THERE ARE, AND CONCERNING MERCENARIES
exclusions: front matter and dedication before THE PRINCE
notes: Chapter 12 shifts from the forms of principalities to the military foundations that keep any state standing.
The attack on mercenaries operates at two levels: the ordinary soldiers are tied only by stipend, and the captains are dangerous whether they are capable or incompetent.
Italy's ruin is explained not only by cowardice but by a whole mercenary system that lowered infantry, minimized danger, and left the peninsula open to sudden loss.
